comments: Aerodynamic drag of the above-water boat that is not a sail: mast, boom, standing rigging, hull topsides and crew, for sail::WindageModule. Element dimensions are not repeated here: the mast section, heights and boom come from rig.json, the wire attachment points from rig.json, the freeboards, beam and LOA from particulars.json, the canoe-body draft from hull_hydro.json and the crew count from mass.json. This file holds the drag coefficients, the wire diameters, the crew areas and the discretisation. Drag of an element is 0.5 rho Cd A |V| V along the apparent wind V at the element's centre, with A the area projected normal to V; the Cd values are ORC VPP Documentation 2023 table 5.10 where it gives one. The ORC rig windage assumes the mainsail is set (MAST-Sail, Cd 0.4 to 0.6); this model always uses the bare-mast Cd, so with sails set the mast drag is overstated by the difference.

strips.method: equal-height strips from the sheer at the mast to the masthead, each with the apparent wind at its own height

cd_front.source: ORC VPP Documentation 2023, table 5.10, MAST-Bare, apparent wind angle 0
cd_front.method: ORC's value is on the front area; ORC's EDM factor for a non-standard section aspect ratio is not applied

cd_side.source: ORC VPP Documentation 2023, table 5.10, MAST-Bare, apparent wind angle 90
cd_side.method: ORC's value is on the side area; the section is the constant mast_section_transverse by mast_section_fore_aft of rig.json, ignoring taper and rake

cd_side.source: standard value for a bluff cylinder or rounded rectangle in cross-flow at Re of 1e4 to 1e5
cd_side.method: ORC folds the boom into the mainsail; here it is a box of rig.json boom_section_depth square and e long

cd_end.source: standard value for a flat blunt end face in axial flow
cd_end.method: applied to the depth by depth end area

cd.method: normal-flow Cd of a wire on its diameter times length times the sine of the angle to the wind

spreader_factor.source: ORC VPP Documentation 2023, eq. 5.33, spreader Factor windage
spreader_factor.method: the wire Cd is multiplied by 1 + this factor to stand for the swept spreaders

forestay_diameter.source: rig.json standing_rigging_wire: uppers, lowers and forestay 4.7 mm
forestay_diameter.method: the furled jib's roller-furling foil is not modelled

upper_shroud_diameter.method: one wire per side from the hounds to the chainplate

intermediate_shroud_diameter.method: one wire per side from the upper spreader height on the mast to the chainplate, a straight line that ignores the spreader tips

lower_shroud_diameter.method: one wire per side from the lower spreader height on the mast to the chainplate; the fore and aft lowers of a real rig are one wire here

backstay_diameter.method: one wire from the masthead to the transom centreline at the aft freeboard; the 3.0 mm lower legs of the split backstay are left out

cd.source: ORC VPP Documentation 2023, table 5.10, HULL, 0.816 at apparent wind angles 0 and 90
cd.method: applied to each topsides panel on its area above the water, projected normal to the wind

panels_per_side.method: each side is this many vertical panels at y = +-beam/2 from the stem to the transom, with freeboard piecewise linear through freeboard_fwd_ffm at the stem, freeboard_at_mast at the mast and freeboard_aft_fam at the transom; the bottom edge is the canoe-body draft tc below the flotation plane, and only the area above the water, found per panel by clipping the rotated panel at world z = 0, is used

cd.method: one box per crew point at the MassModel crew position, areas per person below times crew_count of mass.json

sitting_front_area_per_person.source: ORC VPP Documentation 2023, table 5.10, CREW reference area at apparent wind angle 0, 0.25
sitting_front_area_per_person.method: ORC gives one figure for the crew; read here as per person, which is an interpretation

sitting_side_area_per_person.source: ORC VPP Documentation 2023, table 5.10, CREW reference area at apparent wind angle 90, 0.5 times the crew mass term
sitting_side_area_per_person.method: the mass term is unclear in the text; 0.5 m^2 per person is used as a seated person's side silhouette

hiking_front_area_per_person.method: the body leans out, so the head-on silhouette widens slightly over the seated one

hiking_side_area_per_person.method: the body leans out and shows less of the side silhouette than a seated one
